<a2ui>
surface("status-list")
filter = segmented_control([{label: "All", value: "all"}, {label: "Done", value: "done"}, {label: "In progress", value: "in_progress"}, {label: "Blocked", value: "blocked"}], "all", "status_filter")
list = entity_list([{name: "Set up project repository", subtitle: "Repository created and access granted to the team.", icon: "📁", status: "Done"}, {name: "Design onboarding flow", subtitle: "Wireframes approved by the product lead.", icon: "🎨", status: "Done"}, {name: "Build authentication", subtitle: "Login and password reset are being implemented.", icon: "🔐", status: "In progress"}, {name: "Write API documentation", subtitle: "Endpoint reference is half complete.", icon: "📝", status: "In progress"}, {name: "Integrate payment gateway", subtitle: "Waiting on credentials from the provider.", icon: "💳", status: "Blocked"}, {name: "Configure CI pipeline", subtitle: "Automated tests now run on every pull request.", icon: "⚙️", status: "Done"}, {name: "Performance testing", subtitle: "Load test scripts are being prepared.", icon: "📈", status: "In progress"}, {name: "Security review", subtitle: "Blocked until the audit slot opens next week.", icon: "🛡️", status: "Blocked"}])
root = columns(2, "2rem", "top", [{blocks: [heading("Project tasks"), body("Eight items. Choose a status to narrow the list."), filter]}, {blocks: [list]}])
</a2ui>

The catalog has no component that filters a list on its own. The segmented control shows the status filter, but it is not wired to the list, so choosing a status won't hide any rows until the host connects the two.
